Same format as lexicon.json: rows are arrays in the order of "fields" (trailing nulls dropped): lemma; id (only for homographs such as "눈#2" snow, else null; gloss_ko.json refers to entries by id||lemma); forms = eojeol as printed (with their particles and endings); pos (n, v, adj, adv, det, pron, num, interj, particle, name, foreign:fr|it|la); gender unused; en = English gloss; ko = short Korean definition; no ipa (Hangul is read as written); level from FrequencyWords ko_50k: the list holds eojeol, so each list entry is analysed (kiwipiepy) to its lemma and the 1/rank weights of all its forms are summed; lemma rank in that summed list (or the best rank of a printed form, if better) gives A1<=500, A2<=1500, B1<=3500, B2<=7000, C1<=15000, else C2 (names and foreign words have none); first, letters as in lexicon.json; example = [tatoeba id, Korean sentence, en translation, null, author] (CC BY 2.0 FR, credit the author, https://tatoeba.org/sentences/show/<id>; the sentence contains the lemma by analysis and its English line shows the gloss); function = 1 for function words. See data/lexicon/README.md. napoleon: every word of the letters (full-text gloss). Rows of the "today's words" cards keep their hand-checked meaning, IPA, pronunciation and example; rows shared with Vincent / Mozart reuse those series' IPA, pronunciation and reviewed example; other rows: meaning written for this letter text (not yet checked by a person), IPA from espeak-ng (approximate), example from Tatoeba.
